blind_target.title: Social identity contingencies: how diversity cues signal threat or safety for African Americans in mainstream institutions
blind_target.evidence_quote: Replication of “Social identity contingencies: How diversity cues signal threat or safety for African Americans in mainstream institutions” by V Purdie-Vaughns, CM Steele, PG Davies, R Ditlmann, JR Crosby (2008, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology). Kathleen Schmidt kes7z@virginia.edu
blind_target.outcome_quote: Confirmatory analyses did not replicate the original finding that fairness cues create more trust for Black but not White participants in an environment with low-minority representation. Exploratory analyses showed a pattern of results in the opposite direction: White participants responded to high fairness cues by feeling more trust to a greater degree than Black participants. The interaction between race and fairness cue did not impact identity contingent evaluations. Data Preparation Data were transposed into short form and cleaned by recoding variables into the appropriate formats.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Individual primary replication report: authors’ verdict and comparisons to this original, prioritizing an overall verdict when stated.
